about: Merged concept map for cs-interview-prep-ultra: one row per concept, merged across the inventories in inventory/. Rows are in spec order (toc.json chapters, with appendix A's concepts where its chapters stood). A concept with an "appendix" field lives on that appendix's pages (curated links, not built as text); its chapter and section ids still name its group and page. treatments list every inventory row that teaches the concept; the judge picks a home later. dropped lists inventory rows that became no concept.

concepts.name: Algorithm
concepts.statement: An algorithm is an explicit, precise, unambiguous, mechanically executable sequence of elementary instructions, usually intended to accomplish a specific purpose.
concepts.notes: Its worked example is jeffe:0.3 (ApportionCongress, the apportionment of Congress), carried whole with jeffe:0.1 (ruling 18, METHOD §4.4) as the home of the apportionment concept in this section (ruling 19); errata 6 and bridge B2 apply.

concepts.name: Underspecified algorithm
concepts.statement: Martin’s “how to become a millionaire and never pay taxes” is not an algorithm, because its first step, get a million dollars, is not an elementary, unambiguous instruction; it is a perfectly good reduction.
aliases: What makes a description not an algorithm

concepts.name: Describing an algorithm
concepts.statement: A complete description of an algorithm gives what (a precise specification of the problem), how (the algorithm itself, loops written as loops and recursion as recursion), why (a proof that it solves the problem) and how fast (an analysis of its running time).
aliases: Describing an algorithm: what, how, why, how fast
concepts.notes: jeffe:0.5 mentions the compass-and-straightedge multiplication of jeffe:0.2 "Compass and Straightedge". That subsection gets no concept row: it is an aside on Euclid's constructions as algorithms that no exercise would test on its own and no interview asks, so it stays context. Ruling 19 (METHOD §4.4): it is carried whole with the 0.2 block of lattice-multiplication (same source, same section), so 0.5's mention needs no bridge (B1 settled).

concepts.name: The need for efficiency
concepts.statement: Scanning every item does not scale: 10^6 searches over 10^6 items is 10^12 inspections, about 1000 seconds at 10^9 operations a second, so a data structure must be organised so that most operations inspect few items.

concepts.name: Interface and implementation
concepts.statement: An interface, or abstract data type, names the operations a data structure supports and what they mean; an implementation gives its internal representation and the algorithms for the operations. One interface can have many implementations.

concepts.name: Lattice multiplication
concepts.statement: Multiplying an m-digit number by an n-digit number by summing the partial products X[i] · Y[j] · 10^(i+j), in whatever order and with whatever handling of the carries, takes O(mn) time, dominated by the single-digit multiplications.

concepts.name: Peasant multiplication
concepts.statement: x · y can be computed with only parity tests, addition, doubling (duplation) and halving (mediation): halve x and double y, adding y to the product whenever x is odd; this takes O(log x) such steps and O(mn) time for an m-digit and an n-digit number.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of binary-exponentiation (core).

concepts.name: Huntington–Hill apportionment
concepts.statement: Huntington–Hill gives each state one representative, then each next seat to the state of highest priority P/√(r(r+1)), held in a priority queue used only through NewPriorityQueue, Insert and ExtractMax; the output, and so its correctness, does not depend on how the queue is implemented.
concepts.notes: Home moved from 9.1 (priority queues) to 1.1 by ruling 19 (METHOD §4.4): jeffe:0.3 is carried whole there as the worked example for algorithm (ruling 18). The running times (O(Rn) with the Census Bureau's unsorted array, O(R log n) with a binary heap) are not in 0.3 but in jeffe:0.6, the complexity-analysis passage of 1.4, so the statement no longer carries the O(R log n) bound; the binary heap that gives it is 9.2. Edge to priority-queue dropped: jeffe:0.3 uses the priority queue as a black box: it names NewPriorityQueue, Insert and ExtractMax in place and says the output does not depend on how the queue is implemented. The implementations and the O(R log n) bound come later (jeffe:0.6 in 1.4; binary heaps in 9.2). Lets Huntington-Hill live in 1.1 (ruling 19).

concepts.name: Logarithms
concepts.statement: log_b k is the unique x with b^x = k; log with no base means log₂, and ln k is log_e k, the natural logarithm, with e ≈ 2.71828. log_b k is roughly the number of times k must be divided by b before the result is at most 1. A logarithm changes base as log_b k = log_a k / log_a b, so ln k = (ln 2)(log k).

concepts.name: Factorials and Stirling’s approximation
concepts.statement: n! = 1·2·…·n counts the orderings of n distinct elements, and 0! = 1. Stirling’s Approximation gives n! = √(2πn)(n/e)ⁿ e^α(n) with 1/(12n + 1) < α(n) < 1/(12n), and so ln(n!) = n ln n − n + ½ ln(2πn) + α(n). The binomial coefficient n!/(k!(n − k)!) counts the k-element subsets of an n-element set.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of comparison-sort-lower-bound (core).

concepts.name: Harmonic numbers
concepts.statement: The k-th harmonic number is H_k = 1 + 1/2 + 1/3 + … + 1/k. It has no simple closed form, but ln k < H_k ≤ ln k + 1 for k ≥ 1, because H_k is the area of k unit-width rectangles that lie over the curve 1/x from 1, or, after the first, under it.

concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.statement: For a function f(n), O(f(n)) is the set of functions g(n) for which there exist c > 0 and n₀ such that g(n) ≤ c·f(n) for all n ≥ n₀: an upper bound on growth, with constant factors and small n set aside.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:big-o, ods:big-oh).

concepts.name: Big-Omega and Big-Theta
concepts.statement: T(n) is in Ω(g(n)) when there exist positive constants c and n₀ such that T(n) ≥ c·g(n) for all n > n₀, a lower bound; it is Θ(h(n)) when it is in both O(h(n)) and Ω(h(n)); and the limit of f(n)/g(n) as n grows (∞, 0 or a constant other than zero) puts f(n) in Ω(g(n)), O(g(n)) or Θ(g(n)).
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:big-omega-theta, wikipedia:Big_O_notation#Family_of_Bachmann–Landau_notations, opendsa:AlgAnal/AnalLower). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Analysis with multiple parameters
concepts.statement: When an algorithm’s cost depends on several parameters, the analysis keeps each one for the steps that depend on it (Θ(P + C log C) for P pixels and C colours) rather than folding them into one input size.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:multivariate-big-oh, opendsa:AlgAnal/AnalMultiple). OpenDSA AnalMultiple is the winner (judgements/ch01-03-reconciled.md); added from the reconciliation pass. Edge to big-omega-theta added: OpenDSA's Multiple Parameters (the winner) states its bound as Θ(P + C log C), so it rests on Θ, which the same section introduces just before it (1.3; synced with book.json in the chapter 1 pass).

concepts.name: The w-bit word-RAM model
concepts.statement: Memory is cells, each holding a w-bit word; arithmetic, comparisons and bitwise operations on words take constant time, any cell is read or written in constant time, allocating a block of k words takes O(k) time, and the only assumption about the word size is w ≥ log n. Space is measured in words.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of multiplicative-hashing (core).

concepts.name: Analysing running time and space
concepts.statement: Measure an algorithm’s running time by counting how often it executes an instruction or reaches a milestone, as a function of its input: nested loops give nested sums, a recursive algorithm a recurrence, and the count may depend on how an underlying data structure is implemented; space and other resources are counted the same way.
aliases: Analysing an algorithm's running time and space
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:complexity-analysis, jeffe:running-time-analysis).

concepts.name: Worst-case, amortized and expected running times
concepts.statement: A worst-case running time f(n) means no single operation ever takes longer than f(n); an amortized running time f(n) means any sequence of m operations takes at most m f(n); an expected running time f(n) means the running time is a random variable, over the data structure’s own random choices, whose expected value is at most f(n).

concepts.name: Amortized analysis
concepts.statement: Amortized analysis bounds the average cost per operation over a worst-case sequence of operations, spreading the cost of occasional expensive operations (a resize) over the cheap ones; it involves no probability.
concepts.notes: Merged 5 rows (ciu:amortized-analysis, jeffe-notes:amortized-cost, wikipedia:Amortized_analysis, opendsa:SeniorAlgAnal/AmortAnal, oiwiki:basic/amortized-analysis#引入). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates. OI Wiki (in translation) is the winner; Winner and locator: judgements/ch01-03-reconciled.md, final winner table.

concepts.name: Aggregate analysis and the accounting method
concepts.statement: Bound the total cost of a sequence of operations by summing it and averaging it over the operations (aggregate analysis), or by charging each operation a fixed amortized cost whose surplus is stored as credit to pay for later expensive operations (the accounting method).
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe-notes:aggregate-accounting, wikipedia:Amortized_analysis#Method, oiwiki:basic/amortized-analysis#记账分析). Source tiers differ (jeffe-notes stretch, wikipedia core, oiwiki core); reconciled to the most common, core. Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates. OI Wiki (in translation) is the winner; Winner and locator: judgements/ch01-03-reconciled.md, final winner table.

concepts.name: Potential method
concepts.statement: Define a potential Φ on the states of a data structure with Φ(S) ≥ Φ(S₀) for every reachable state; an operation’s amortized cost is its actual cost plus the change in Φ, and the total amortized cost of any sequence bounds its total actual cost.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe-notes:potential-method, ods:potential-method, oiwiki:basic/amortized-analysis#势能分析). OI Wiki (in translation) is the winner; Winner and locator: judgements/ch01-03-reconciled.md, final winner table. Edge to dynamic-array-cost dropped: ODS states the potential method inside its DualArrayDeque lemma; the method itself rests on amortized analysis, not on array resizing. Keeps amortized analysis in chapter 1 as CIU orders it.

concepts.name: Factorials, permutations and combinations
concepts.statement: If a whole can be divided into k parts with n_i choices for the i-th part, there are n₁ × n₂ × … × n_k ways of doing the whole; so there are n! orderings of n items, n!/(n − k)! ordered selections of k of them, and (n choose k) = n!/((n − k)! k!) unordered ones.
aliases: The fundamental theorem of counting (product rule)
concepts.notes: Merged 6 rows (ciu:counting, dmoi3:sec_counting-combperm, oiwiki:math/combinatorics/combination#排列与组合基础, brisk:counting#The_Fundamental_Theorem, brisk:counting#Permutations, brisk:counting#Combinations). concepts.name: Basic probability
concepts.statement: The outcomes form the sample space Ω and an event is a subset of it; a probability measure Pr gives each event a number in [0, 1] with Pr(Ω) = 1, Pr(A) ≥ 0 and Pr(A ∪ B) = Pr(A) + Pr(B) − Pr(A ∩ B). When all N outcomes are equally likely, Pr(A) = |A|/N.
aliases: Sample spaces by the four-step method
Probability spaces and events (for algorithm analysis)
Rules of probability for two events

concepts.name: Conditional probability and independence
concepts.statement: Pr(A|K) = Pr(A ∩ K)/Pr(K) is the probability of A once K is known to have occurred; A and B are independent when Pr(A|B) = Pr(A), so that knowing one tells nothing about the other.

concepts.name: Random variable
concepts.statement: A random variable R on a probability space is a total function whose domain is the sample space, usually real-valued: every outcome determines its value, and an assertion about its value, such as [C = 2], is an event.
concepts.notes: Merged 8 rows (mcs2018:19.1, wikibooks:Probability/Random_Variables#Definition, aspnes-202:12.2, aspnes-469:3, wikipedia:Random_variable, openintro-stats:3.4, appcomb:s_probability_discrete-random-variables, oiwiki:math/probability/random-variable#随机变量). concepts.name: Expected value and linearity of expectation
concepts.statement: The expected value of a discrete random variable is E[X] = Σ_x x·Pr{X = x}; for any random variables, E[X + Y] = E[X] + E[Y] and E[Σ X_i] = Σ E[X_i], so a complicated random variable can be broken into a sum of simpler ones.
aliases: Random variables and linearity of expectation
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe-notes:linearity-of-expectation, ods:linearity-of-expectation, ciu:random-variables-expectation). Edge to random-variable added: expectation is defined on random variables, which ODS's winning passage uses undefined (ruling 18).

concepts.name: Indicator random variables
concepts.statement: Write a count as a sum of indicator variables I_i, each 1 if its event happens and 0 otherwise; then E[Σ I_i] = Σ Pr{I_i = 1}, as for the k/2 expected heads in k fair tosses.

concepts.name: Expected tosses until the first head
concepts.statement: If T is the number of times a fair coin is tossed up to and including the first time it comes up heads, then E[T] = 2.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of build-heap (core).

concepts.name: Array
concepts.statement: A fixed-size block of contiguous memory holding items of one size, so any index is reached in O(1) by address arithmetic; includes multi-dimensional and jagged arrays.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:array, wikipedia:Array_(data_structure), wikibooks:Data_Structures/Arrays). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates. Assumes, untaught in the map: memory and pointers.

concepts.name: Indexing by pointer arithmetic
concepts.statement: Reach an array element by adding an offset to the base pointer instead of using index syntax.

concepts.name: List interface (linear sequence)
concepts.statement: A List represents x_0,...,x_{n-1} with size(), get(i), set(i,x), add(i,x) (shifting x_i..x_{n-1} right) and remove(i) (shifting left). It subsumes Deque: addFirst(x)=add(0,x), removeLast()=remove(size()-1), etc.
concepts.notes: Edge to deque dropped: ODS introduces List as a generalisation of Deque; a list does not need the deque interface. Otherwise lists would wait for stacks and queues.

concepts.name: Dynamic array (vector)
concepts.statement: An array that grows by allocating a larger block (CIU: double the capacity when full) and shrinks (halve when size falls to a quarter), separating size from capacity.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:dynamic-array, ods:arraystack).

concepts.name: Growing and shrinking the backing array
concepts.statement: resize() allocates an array of size 2n and copies the n elements, taking O(n) time; add calls it when the array is full and remove calls it when a.length >= 3n.

concepts.name: Cost of dynamic-array operations
concepts.statement: Appending or removing at the end, indexing and updating are O(1) (append amortized over resizes); inserting or deleting elsewhere is O(n) because items shift; space is O(n) even at 2n capacity.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:dynamic-array-cost, ods:arraystack-amortized-resize).

concepts.name: Block copying with memcpy/arraycopy
concepts.statement: Replace element-by-element shift and copy loops with native block moves (memcpy/memmove, std::copy, System.arraycopy); asymptotics are unchanged but the book measured speedups of 2 to 3 times.

concepts.name: Implement a vector
concepts.statement: Build a resizable array on raw memory with size, capacity, is_empty, at, push, insert, prepend, pop, delete, remove, find and a private resize.
concepts.notes: Stays "no open prose": open sources give implementations, not prose (confirmed by the chapter 2 finder run). Its explanation in judgements/ch02.md is the ODS ArrayStack code as shown in the 2.2 passages, with no separate prose block.

concepts.name: Two pointers
concepts.statement: Two indices move through an array, together or toward each other, so that each step rules out candidates and the scan ends after one O(n) pass with O(1) extra space; on a sorted array, closing in from both ends on a target pair sum is the classic case.
aliases: Two pointers on a sorted sequence
Pair sum in a sorted array by two pointers
Container with most water by two pointers

concepts.name: 3SUM in quadratic time
concepts.statement: Sort the array; for each a[i], look for a pair summing to -a[i] in the rest with two pointers moving inward by the sign of the sum, giving O(n^2) time.
aliases: 3SUM by sorting and two pointers, skipping duplicates
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (wikipedia:3SUM#Quadratic_algorithm, doocs-leetcode:0015#Solution_1:_Sort_+_Two_Pointers). From the gap-patterns finder run (dossiers/gap-patterns.md §1). Sorting is used as a library call here; sorting algorithms are chapter 10.

concepts.name: Merging two sorted lists
concepts.statement: Two sorted lists are merged by keeping one pointer in each and repeatedly moving the smaller head to the output, in time linear in the total length.
concepts.notes: From the gap-patterns finder run (dossiers/gap-patterns.md §1): two pointers, one per sorted list. Merge sort (10.3) rests on it (edge added).

concepts.name: Fixed-size sliding window
concepts.statement: A window of the last k items is updated in O(1) per step by adding the item that enters and subtracting the one that leaves (SMA_next = SMA_prev + (p_new - p_old)/k), instead of recomputing all k.
aliases: Maximum average subarray of length k
Most vowels in a substring of length k
Permutation in a string by a window of counts
All anagram windows of a pattern

concepts.name: Variable-size sliding window
concepts.statement: Extend the window at the right one element at a time and shrink it from the left while it breaks the condition (here: a repeated character, tracked in a set), so each element enters and leaves once and the longest valid window is found in O(n).
aliases: Maintaining window information with two pointers

concepts.name: Prefix sums
concepts.statement: The prefix sums of x_0, x_1, ... are y_i = x_0 + ... + x_i, computed in one pass by y_i = y_{i-1} + x_i; with them any range sum is a difference of two prefix sums, and finite differences invert them.
aliases: Range sum query with a leading zero
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (wikipedia:Prefix_sum, oiwiki:basic/prefix-sum#一维前缀和, doocs-leetcode:0303#Solution_1:_Prefix_Sum). From the gap-patterns finder run (dossiers/gap-patterns.md §4). Replaces the bracketed [prefix sums] that Fenwick trees, sqrt decomposition and the prefix-minimum maximum subarray assumed.

concepts.name: Two-dimensional prefix sums (summed-area table)
concepts.statement: I(x, y) = i(x, y) + I(x, y-1) + I(x-1, y) - I(x-1, y-1) builds the table in one pass, after which the sum over any axis-aligned rectangle takes four lookups by inclusion-exclusion.
aliases: Range sum query 2D by prefix sums
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (wikipedia:Summed-area_table#The_algorithm, oiwiki:basic/prefix-sum#基于容斥原理, doocs-leetcode:0304#Solution_1:_Two-dimensional_Prefix_Sum). From the gap-patterns finder run (dossiers/gap-patterns.md §4). Tier stretch: range sums over a matrix come up at harder interviews and in contests, not in the typical loop, and no open exercise with tests was found for it.

concepts.name: Difference arrays
concepts.statement: The difference array b_i = a_i - a_{i-1} is the inverse of prefix sums: adding v to a_l..a_r becomes b_l += v and b_{r+1} -= v, so many range updates cost O(1) each and one prefix-sum pass recovers the array.
aliases: Range addition by a difference array
Car pooling by a difference array over positions
Flight bookings by a difference array

concepts.name: Two-dimensional difference arrays
concepts.statement: Adding v to every cell of a sub-rectangle becomes four point updates of a 2D difference array (+v, -v, -v, +v at the corners), and a 2D prefix-sum pass recovers the matrix.
concepts.notes: From the gap-patterns finder run (dossiers/gap-patterns.md §4; OI Wiki only). Tier stretch, as 2D prefix sums.

concepts.name: Singly linked list
concepts.statement: A sequence of nodes, each holding a value and a pointer to the next node, reached from a head pointer (optionally also a tail pointer).

concepts.name: Linked lists versus arrays
concepts.statement: Lists give O(1) insertion/removal at a known node but O(n) indexing and poor cache locality; arrays give O(1) indexing and locality but O(n) middle insertion, so arrays usually win in practice.

concepts.name: Dummy (sentinel) node
concepts.statement: A DLList keeps a dummy node whose next is the first node and prev is the last, making the list circular so insertion and removal have no special cases for empty lists or the ends.

concepts.name: Doubly linked list
concepts.statement: A linked list whose nodes also point to their predecessor, allowing O(1) removal of a known node and backward traversal.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:doubly-linked-list, ods:dllist).

concepts.name: Floyd's cycle detection (tortoise and hare)
concepts.statement: Move one pointer one step and another two steps at a time; they meet iff the linked list has a cycle, within O(length) steps.

concepts.name: Finding where the cycle starts
concepts.statement: After the pointers meet, reset one to the head and advance both one step at a time; they meet at the cycle's first node.

concepts.name: Why the reset finds the cycle start
concepts.statement: With a steps to the cycle and length L, the meeting point satisfies a + b = (y - 2x)L, so walking a more steps from it lands on the cycle start.

concepts.name: Stack
concepts.statement: A last-in, first-out collection with push, pop and peek, each O(1) when backed by an array or linked list.

concepts.name: Balanced bracket sequence
concepts.statement: The empty string is balanced, and if s and t are balanced then so are (s) and st.

concepts.name: Checking bracket balance
concepts.statement: With one bracket type, a depth counter that never goes negative and ends at 0 suffices; with several types, a stack must match each closing bracket with the most recent unmatched opening one.

concepts.name: Queue
concepts.statement: A first-in, first-out collection: enqueue at the tail, dequeue at the front.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:queue, ods:queue-interface).

concepts.name: Circular buffer
concepts.statement: A fixed-size array used as a ring, with read and write indices that wrap around, giving a bounded FIFO queue.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:circular-buffer, ods:circular-array).

concepts.name: Queue on a linked list with a tail pointer
concepts.statement: Implement enqueue at the tail and dequeue at the head in O(1); enqueuing at the head and dequeuing at the tail would make dequeue O(n).

concepts.name: ArrayQueue (array-backed FIFO queue)
concepts.statement: An ArrayQueue keeps head index j and count n in a circular array; add(x) writes a[(j+n)%a.length], remove() takes a[j] and advances j, both O(1) ignoring resize(), with O(m) total resize cost over m operations.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:arrayqueue, ciu:queue-fixed-array). CIU's fixed-size array queue and ODS's resizing ArrayQueue are one concept (a circular array holding a FIFO queue); ODS adds resizing.

concepts.name: Deque interface
concepts.statement: A Deque is a sequence with a front and back supporting addFirst(x), removeFirst(), addLast(x), removeLast(); a Stack uses addFirst/removeFirst and a FIFO Queue uses addLast/removeFirst.

concepts.name: ArrayDeque
concepts.statement: An ArrayDeque is a circular-array List that shifts whichever side of position i is shorter, so get/set take O(1) and add(i,x)/remove(i) take O(1+min{i, n-i}) ignoring resize(); all Deque operations are O(1) amortized.

concepts.name: DualArrayDeque: a deque from two stacks
concepts.statement: Two ArrayStacks, front (stored reversed) and back, back to back; balance() rebalances to floor(n/2)/ceil(n/2) when either holds fewer than n/4 elements. get/set O(1), add/remove O(1+min{i,n-i}), with O(m) total balance() cost.

concepts.name: Minimum stack
concepts.statement: Store each stack entry as a pair (value, minimum of this entry and everything below it); the stack minimum is then the top pair's second field, and push/pop stay O(1).

concepts.name: Queue from two stacks (with minimum)
concepts.statement: Push to stack s1 and pop from stack s2, moving all of s1 into s2 when s2 is empty; each element moves once, so all operations are amortised O(1), and with minimum stacks the queue minimum is the smaller of the two stack minima.

concepts.name: Minimum queue via a monotonic deque
concepts.statement: Keep only the elements that can still become the minimum, in non-decreasing order: before pushing x, remove trailing elements larger than x; the head is the minimum and every element is pushed and popped at most once, so operations are amortised O(1). Removal needs the value (method 1) or stored indices (method 2).

concepts.name: Sliding window minimum
concepts.statement: The minimum of every length-M subarray of an array of length N can be found in O(N) total by sliding a minimum queue along the array.
aliases: minimum of all subarrays of fixed length
Sliding window maximum with a monotonic deque

concepts.name: Nearest smaller element to the left/right with a stack
concepts.statement: Scan the row keeping a stack of indices with increasing values, popping while the top is not smaller; the remaining top is the nearest smaller (here: larger d) index, O(m) per row amortised.
aliases: All nearest smaller values by a stack

concepts.name: Largest zero submatrix in O(nm)
concepts.statement: For each cell compute d[i][j], the nearest row above with a 1; then in each row the widest rectangle bounded by d is found with a monotonic stack (nearest larger d to left and right), giving O(nm) time and O(m) memory.

concepts.name: Reverse Polish notation evaluation
concepts.statement: Evaluate postfix expressions with one stack: push operands, and for an operator pop its arguments and push the result, in O(n).

concepts.name: Infix expression parsing with two stacks
concepts.statement: Keep an operand stack and an operator stack in strictly decreasing priority; on each operator first apply stacked operators of higher (or equal, for left-associative) priority, handling parentheses as barriers; evaluates in O(n).

concepts.name: Unary and right-associative operators in parsing
concepts.statement: An operator is unary if it follows another operator, an opening parenthesis or nothing; right-associative operators are postponed when priorities are equal.

concepts.name: RootishArrayStack
concepts.statement: Store the list in r blocks of sizes 1, 2, ..., r; element i lives in block b where b(b+1)/2 <= i < (b+1)(b+2)/2. get/set O(1), add/remove O(1+n-i), O(m) total grow/shrink, and only O(sqrt n) wasted space.

concepts.name: Block index by the quadratic formula
concepts.statement: Block b holds index i when b is the smallest integer with (b+1)(b+2)/2 >= i+1, so i2b(i) = ceil((-3 + sqrt(9 + 8i))/2) by the quadratic formula. Because square root is not a word-RAM primitive, the section shows floor(sqrt x) for x <= n in O(1) time after O(sqrt n) preprocessing into two lookup arrays (lem:root).

concepts.name: Omega(sqrt n) wasted space is unavoidable
concepts.statement: Any structure that starts empty and adds items one at a time into allocated blocks must at some moment waste at least sqrt(n) space (either many blocks with overhead, or a large block not yet full), so RootishArrayStack is optimal.

concepts.name: SEList (space-efficient list)
concepts.statement: A DLList of blocks, each a bounded deque (BDeque) of capacity b+1 holding b-1 to b+1 elements (except the last). Ignoring spread/gather, get/set take O(1+min{i,n-i}/b) and add/remove O(b+min{i,n-i}/b), and wasted space is only O(b+n/b), close to the sqrt(n) lower bound when b is about sqrt(n).

concepts.name: SEList spreading and gathering
concepts.statement: When a run of b blocks is full, spread(u) adds a block; when b blocks are nearly empty, gather(u) removes one. By the potential method (potential = number of fragile blocks) any m add/remove operations spend O(bm) total time in spread and gather.

concepts.name: Reduction
concepts.statement: Reducing problem X to problem Y means solving X with an algorithm for Y used as a black box; correctness of the X algorithm may not depend on how Y is solved.

concepts.name: Recursion: simplify and delegate (the Recursion Fairy)
concepts.statement: Solve small instances directly; otherwise reduce to strictly simpler instances of the same problem and trust the recursive calls (the induction hypothesis); every chain of reductions must reach a base case.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe:recursion, ciu:recursion).

concepts.name: Tail recursion
concepts.statement: A recursive call that is the function's last action, which a compiler can turn into a loop so stack space stays constant.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:tail-recursion, wikipedia:Tail_call). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Tower of Hanoi
concepts.statement: Move the top n-1 disks to the spare peg, move the largest disk, move the n-1 disks back on top; this takes T(n)=2T(n-1)+1 = 2^n - 1 moves, which is optimal.

concepts.name: Binary exponentiation
concepts.statement: Writing the exponent n in binary and squaring repeatedly, a^n is the product of the squares a^(2^i) for the set bits of n, so it takes O(log n) multiplications instead of O(n).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (cpa:binary-exponentiation, jeffe:fast-exponentiation).

concepts.name: Iterative binary exponentiation
concepts.statement: The loop version keeps a running square of a, multiplies it into the result whenever the low bit of n is set, and shifts n right; it does the same work as the recursion without call overhead.

concepts.name: Modular exponentiation
concepts.statement: Because (a*b) mod m = ((a mod m)(b mod m)) mod m, x^n mod m is computed by binary exponentiation with every multiplication reduced mod m.
concepts.notes: Assumes, untaught in the map: modular arithmetic.

concepts.name: Binary exponentiation for any associative operation
concepts.statement: The squaring trick needs only associativity, so it applies to modular multiplication, matrix multiplication, permutation composition and other monoids, not just numbers.

concepts.name: Proof by smallest counterexample
concepts.statement: To prove P(n) for all n, suppose some n fails and take the smallest such n; deriving a smaller counterexample is a contradiction (shown by proving every integer > 1 has a prime divisor).

concepts.name: The axiom of induction and strong induction
concepts.statement: If P(0) holds and P(k) for all k < n implies P(n), then P(n) holds for all natural numbers; the inductive hypothesis may assume all smaller cases (strong induction).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe-notes:induction-axiom, csci30:correctness#Mathematical_induction). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Induction on numbers, summations and tilings
concepts.statement: Worked induction proofs: closed forms for summations, tiling a 2^n x 2^n board minus one square with L-triominoes, existence of binary representations, Fibonacci parity.

concepts.name: Induction on recursive functions and trees
concepts.statement: Properties of recursively defined functions and of trees are proved by induction following the recursive definition (e.g. on the subtrees of a full binary tree).

concepts.name: Proving an algorithm correct
concepts.statement: Correctness must hold for every input and must be proved, usually by induction; 'obvious' is often a synonym for 'wrong'.

concepts.name: USet interface (unordered set)
concepts.statement: A USet holds n distinct elements in no order, with size(), add(x) (returns false if an equal element exists), remove(x) and find(x), which returns the stored element y equal to x or null.

concepts.name: Dictionary/map as a USet of pairs
concepts.statement: A map is a USet of (key, value) Pairs that compare equal when their keys are equal; find((k,null)) returns the stored (k,v), recovering v from k.

concepts.name: Hash table
concepts.statement: A map that stores key-value pairs in an array of buckets chosen by a hash function of the key, giving expected O(1) lookup, insert and delete.
concepts.notes: Merged 4 rows (ciu:hash-table, jeffe-notes:hash-table, wikipedia:Hash_table, opendsa:Hashing/HashIntro). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Hashing with chaining
concepts.statement: Each bucket holds a list of colliding entries; with a good hash and load factor alpha, operations cost expected O(1+alpha).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:hashing-with-chaining, ods:hashing-with-chaining). Split from jeffe-notes 05-hashing.4, whose row is the expected-chain-length analysis (concept chaining-analysis). Edge to multiplicative-hashing dropped: ODS's ChainedHashTable happens to use multiplicative hashing; chaining works with any hash function.

concepts.name: Table doubling
concepts.statement: Resize the table (and rehash) when the load factor passes a threshold, keeping operations O(1) amortized.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:table-doubling, wikipedia:Hash_table#Dynamic_resizing). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Open addressing and linear probing
concepts.statement: Collisions are resolved inside the array itself by probing a sequence of slots (linear probing: the next slot), with deletions needing care.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:open-addressing, ods:open-addressing-linear-probing, jeffe-notes:open-addressing).

concepts.name: Deleted markers (tombstones) in open addressing
concepts.statement: Entries are data, null (never used) or del (once used, now deleted); remove(x) writes del rather than null so later searches do not stop early, and add may reuse a del slot. Counter q tracks data plus del entries, and resize() clears the del entries.

concepts.name: Implement a hash table with linear probing
concepts.statement: Build hash(k,m), add (updating an existing key), exists, get and remove on an array using linear probing.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:implement-hash-table, sdp:ood-hash-map). sdp's OOD hash-map notebook is the same exercise as CIU's implementation task.

concepts.name: Universal hash families
concepts.statement: Any fixed hash function has bad inputs, so h is chosen at random from a family; the family is universal if Pr[h(x)=h(y)] <= 1/m for all x != y.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe-notes:universal-hashing, ciu:universal-perfect-hashing, wikipedia:Hash_function#Universality). Tier from CIU (required list); other sources say jeffe-notes stretch, wikipedia core. ciu:universal-perfect-hashing also treats perfect-hashing (row split by granularity). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates. CIU's one row covers universal and perfect hashing; split into two concepts, CIU's row treats both.

concepts.name: Multiplicative hashing
concepts.statement: With t.length = 2^d and z a random odd w-bit integer, hash(x) = ((z*x) mod 2^w) div 2^{w-d}, i.e. the top d bits of z*x computed with overflow and a right shift. For x != y, Pr{hash(x) = hash(y)} <= 2/2^d.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:multiplicative-hashing, jeffe-notes:multiplicative-hashing). Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of hash-compound (core).

concepts.name: Tabulation hashing
concepts.statement: Split the w-bit hash code into w/r chunks of r bits, look each up in its own table of 2^r random w-bit integers, and XOR the results; this gives hash values strong enough for the linear probing analysis without a 2^w-entry table.

concepts.name: Perfect hashing (two-level)
concepts.statement: For a static set, hash into n primary buckets and give each bucket of size n_i a collision-free secondary table of size n_i^2; expected total space is O(n) and lookups take O(1) worst-case time.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe-notes:perfect-hashing, ciu:universal-perfect-hashing). Tier from CIU (required list); other sources say jeffe-notes contest. ciu:universal-perfect-hashing also treats universal-hashing (row split by granularity).

concepts.name: Hash code requirements
concepts.statement: A hash code maps objects to w-bit integers so that equal objects get equal codes and unequal objects collide with small probability, close to 1/2^w.

concepts.name: Hash codes for primitive types
concepts.statement: A value of at most w bits uses its own bit pattern as its hash code; a value of c*w bits (e.g. Java long/double) is treated as a compound object of c parts.

concepts.name: Hash codes for compound objects
concepts.statement: Combine part hash codes x_0..x_{r-1} as ((z * sum z_i x_i) mod 2^{2w}) div 2^w with independent random w-bit z_i and a random odd 2w-bit z (a final multiplicative-hashing step), rather than easily foiled XOR hacks; tuples differing in some part collide with probability at most 3/2^w.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of polynomial-hash (core).

concepts.name: Expected chain length under universal hashing
concepts.statement: With each slot holding a linked list and h drawn from a universal family, the expected length of the chain for any key is at most 1 + n/m, so operations take O(1 + n/m) expected time.

concepts.name: Balls and bins: maximum chain length
concepts.statement: Throwing n balls into n bins uniformly, the fullest bin holds O(log n / log log n) balls with high probability.

concepts.name: Analysis of linear probing via runs
concepts.statement: Assuming independent uniform hash values, the probability that a run of length k starts at a given slot is O(c^k) for a constant c < 1, so the expected run containing a slot has constant length.
concepts.notes: Edge to random-variable added: it bounds the expected length of a run, a random variable over the hash values (ruling 18).

concepts.name: Cuckoo hashing
concepts.statement: Each key lives in one of two slots h1(x) or h2(x); insertion evicts occupants along a path and rebuilds on long cycles, giving worst-case O(1) lookups and expected O(1) insertions at load below 1/2.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe-notes:cuckoo-hashing, wikipedia:Hash_table#Cuckoo_hashing). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: LRU cache: hash map plus doubly linked list
concepts.statement: An LRU cache keeps a hash map from key to node and a doubly linked list ordered by recency: get moves the node to the front; set updates and moves an existing node, or at capacity evicts the tail node (and its map entry) before inserting the new node at the front.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (sdp:lru-cache, ciu:lru-cache, sdp:ood-lru-cache). sdp's query-cache implementation and its OOD LRU notebook are the same structure CIU asks for under Caches.

concepts.name: Binary search
concepts.statement: On a sorted array, comparing with the middle element and discarding half each step finds a target or its absence in O(log n) comparisons.
aliases: Binary search in a sorted array
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:binary-search, cpa:binary-search).

concepts.name: Half-open interval invariant for binary search
concepts.statement: Keeping A_L <= k < A_R (with virtual A_-1 = -inf, A_n = +inf) and shrinking until R = L + 1 avoids off-by-one errors; M = L + (R-L)/2 avoids overflow.

concepts.name: Lower bound and upper bound
concepts.statement: lower_bound(k) is the first position with A_i >= k and upper_bound(k) the first with A_i > k; together they bound the range of elements equal to k.

concepts.name: Implement binary search, iteratively and recursively
concepts.statement: Write binary search on a sorted integer array both with a loop and with recursion.

concepts.name: Binary search on a monotone predicate
concepts.statement: Any monotone boolean f on 0..n-1 has a single 0-to-1 boundary that binary search finds in O(log n) evaluations of f.
aliases: Binary search as a general template
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (cpa:binary-search-predicate, ciu:binary-search-template).

concepts.name: Binary search on the answer
concepts.statement: When it is easier to check "is the answer at least x?" than to compute the answer, binary search over x with that check as the predicate.

concepts.name: Binary search by descending powers of two
concepts.statement: Advance a pointer by 2^k whenever the predicate is still 0 at i + 2^k, for k from high to low; this is the form used for binary lifting and Fenwick-tree descent.

concepts.name: Parallel binary search
concepts.statement: Advance the binary searches of all queries in lockstep, one level per round, processing query midpoints in sorted order so each round shares one sweep of the data (with a Fenwick or segment tree); the meteors example runs in O((N+K) log N log K).

concepts.name: Bisection on real numbers
concepts.statement: For continuous f on [L, R] the intermediate value theorem guarantees a solution of f(x) = y, and halving the interval a fixed number of times (or to precision eps) finds it.
concepts.notes: Assumes, untaught in the map: intermediate value theorem.

concepts.name: Unimodal function
concepts.statement: f increases then decreases on [l, r] (or the reverse), with a single maximum point or plateau.

concepts.name: Ternary search
concepts.statement: Comparing f at two interior points m1 < m2 rules out [l, m1] or [m2, r] for a unimodal f, so the extremum is found in O(log((r-l)/eps)) evaluations.

concepts.name: Ternary search over integers
concepts.statement: On integers, stop when r - l < 3 and check the remaining points directly; for strictly unimodal integer functions binary search on f(m) < f(m+1) also works.

concepts.name: Golden-section search
concepts.statement: Placing m1, m2 in the golden ratio lets one evaluation be reused each iteration, cutting function evaluations per step to one.

concepts.name: Powers of two and machine words
concepts.statement: Know powers of 2 from 2^1 to 2^16 and 2^32, and that a word is the processor's natural unit of data.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:powers-of-two-words, sdp:powers-of-two). sdp's powers-of-two table (for estimation) and CIU's powers of two are one fact table; it lives here and system design points back to it.

concepts.name: Binary representation and two's complement
concepts.statement: An integer is a sum of a_i 2^i; fixed-width signed integers use two's complement, where -x = ~x + 1.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (cpa:binary-representation, ciu:twos-complement). Edge to bitwise-operators dropped: CIU teaches two's complement through bitwise NOT; the representation does not need the operators (cpa makes the operators depend on the representation). Breaks a cycle.

concepts.name: Bitwise operators
concepts.statement: AND, OR, XOR, NOT and left/right shift act on the bits of an integer; masks combine them to test, set, clear and toggle bits.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:bitwise-operators, cpa:bitwise-operators).

concepts.name: Shift operators
concepts.statement: x >> k is floor division by 2^k and x << k is multiplication by 2^k (within the word width).

concepts.name: Setting, clearing, flipping and testing a bit
concepts.statement: n | (1<<x) sets bit x, n & ~(1<<x) clears it, n ^ (1<<x) flips it, and (n >> x) & 1 reads it.

concepts.name: Power-of-two and divisibility-by-2^k tests
concepts.statement: n > 0 is a power of two iff n & (n-1) = 0, and n is divisible by 2^k iff n & ((1<<k)-1) = 0.

concepts.name: Lowest-set-bit tricks
concepts.statement: n & (n-1) clears the lowest set bit, n & -n isolates it, and n & (n+1) / n | (n+1) clear trailing ones / set the lowest clear bit.

concepts.name: Branch-free bit tricks
concepts.statement: Swap two values with XOR and compute an absolute value with shifts and XOR, without branches.

concepts.name: Counting set bits
concepts.statement: Count the 1 bits of an integer, e.g. by repeatedly clearing the lowest set bit with x & (x-1).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:count-set-bits, cpa:kernighan-popcount).

concepts.name: Counting set bits over 0..n
concepts.statement: Numbers below 2^x contain x*2^(x-1) ones, so the total for 0..n follows from the highest set bit recursively in O(log n).

concepts.name: Enumerating submasks
concepts.statement: s = (s-1) & m steps through all submasks of m in decreasing order, visiting 2^popcount(m) of them; the empty submask needs separate handling.

concepts.name: All masks with all submasks is O(3^n)
concepts.statement: Each bit is either absent from m, in m but not s, or in both, so iterating every submask of every n-bit mask takes 3^n steps in total.
concepts.notes: Assumes, untaught in the map: bitmask DP.

concepts.name: Gray code
concepts.statement: An ordering of binary numbers in which consecutive values differ in exactly one bit.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (cpa:gray-code, jeffe-notes:gray-codes).

concepts.name: G(n) = n xor (n >> 1)
concepts.statement: Bit i of G(n) is set exactly when bits i and i+1 of n differ, so G(n) = n ^ (n >> 1).

concepts.name: Inverse Gray code
concepts.statement: n is recovered from g by prefix xor from the top bit down: n_i = g_i xor n_{i+1}.

concepts.name: Applications of Gray codes
concepts.statement: Gray codes trace a Hamiltonian cycle on the hypercube, reduce sensor and DAC errors, and give the move order in the Towers of Hanoi.

concepts.name: Floating-point representation
concepts.statement: A real number is stored as sign, exponent and mantissa (shown with a simple 8-bit format), which limits range and precision.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:floating-point, lt-csbu:2.2). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Endianness
concepts.statement: Big-endian stores a multi-byte value's most significant byte at the lowest address; little-endian stores the least significant byte first.

concepts.name: Unicode and character encodings
concepts.statement: Unicode assigns code points to characters; encodings such as UTF-8 and UTF-16 map them to bytes, and text is meaningless without knowing its encoding.

concepts.name: Tree
concepts.statement: A connected acyclic structure of nodes with one root, where each node has children; binary trees have at most two.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:tree, wikipedia:Tree_(abstract_data_type), opendsa:General/GenTreeIntro). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Binary tree terminology
concepts.statement: A rooted, ordered binary tree: root, parent, left/right child, depth (path length to the root), ancestor/descendant, subtree, height (longest path to a descendant), leaf. External nodes fill every missing child; a tree with n >= 1 nodes has n+1 external nodes.
concepts.notes: Edge to tree added: ODS's binary-tree terminology and CIU's tree are taught by different sources; a binary tree is a tree.

concepts.name: Recursive binary-tree algorithms
concepts.statement: Nodes store left, right and parent (nil when absent). depth(u) follows parent pointers; size(u) = 1 + size(u.left) + size(u.right) and height(u) = 1 + max(height(u.left), height(u.right)), with nil giving size 0 and height -1.

concepts.name: Depth-first tree traversals: preorder, inorder, postorder
concepts.statement: Recursive traversal visiting self before (pre), between (in) or after (post) the children takes O(n) time and O(height) stack space.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:tree-dfs-orders, ods:traversal-orders).

concepts.name: Non-recursive traversal with parent pointers
concepts.statement: Recursion depth equals tree height and can overflow the stack; instead decide the next step from where you came: from the parent go left, from the left child go right, from the right child go up. Without parent pointers, keep an explicit stack.

concepts.name: Level-order (breadth-first) tree traversal
concepts.statement: Visiting a tree level by level with a queue takes O(n) time and O(width) extra space (O(n) worst case).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:tree-bfs, ods:breadth-first-traversal).

concepts.name: SSet interface and successor search
concepts.statement: An SSet stores elements from a total order, compared with compare(x,y) (<0, >0, =0). Its find(x) returns the smallest y >= x (successor search), giving a meaningful answer even when x is absent.

concepts.name: Prefer USet unless order is needed
concepts.statement: SSet functionality usually costs logarithmic time and more complex code, while a hash-table USet finds in constant expected time; use a USet unless the extra SSet functionality is truly needed.

concepts.name: Binary search tree
concepts.statement: A binary tree in which every key in a node's left subtree is smaller and every key in its right subtree is larger.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:bst, ods:bst-property).

concepts.name: BST search and successor search
concepts.statement: findEQ(x) walks from the root, going left if x < u.x and right if x > u.x; find(x) also remembers the last node z where it went left, returning z.x as the smallest value >= x when x is absent. Cost is proportional to the path length.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:bst-search, ciu:bst-search-insert). ciu:bst-search-insert also treats bst-insert (row split by granularity). CIU joins search and insertion in one row; ODS separates them. Split to ODS's grain, CIU's row treats both.

concepts.name: BST insertion
concepts.statement: add(x) uses findLast(x) to reach the node p where the search ends and attaches a new leaf as p's left or right child (addChild), refusing duplicates.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:bst-add, ciu:bst-search-insert). ciu:bst-search-insert also treats bst-search (row split by granularity).

concepts.name: BST minimum, maximum and height
concepts.statement: The minimum is the leftmost node, the maximum the rightmost; height is computed recursively as 1 + the larger child height.

concepts.name: Inorder successor in a BST
concepts.statement: The next-larger key is the leftmost node of the right subtree, or else the nearest ancestor of which the node lies in the left subtree.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:bst-successor, wikipedia:Binary_search_tree#Successor_and_predecessor). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: BST deletion
concepts.statement: Delete a node by cases: leaf, one child (splice it out), two children (replace with inorder successor or predecessor and delete that).
aliases: BST deletion via splice and successor
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:bst-delete, ods:bst-remove).

concepts.name: Checking whether a binary tree is a BST
concepts.statement: Verify the BST property by passing down allowed (min, max) bounds, or by checking an inorder traversal is increasing.

concepts.name: Implement a BST
concepts.statement: Build insert, get_node_count, print_values, delete_tree, is_in_tree, get_height, get_min, get_max, is_binary_search_tree, delete_value and get_successor.

concepts.name: Cost of an unbalanced BST
concepts.statement: A BinarySearchTree implements SSet with add, remove and find in O(n) time per operation, because their cost is the length of a root-to-node path, which can be n for skewed trees; this motivates balanced variants.

concepts.name: Balanced search trees (the general idea)
concepts.statement: Self-balancing BSTs restructure on insert and delete (rotations, splits) so height stays O(log n) and every operation stays O(log n).
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:balanced-bst-idea, wikipedia:Self-balancing_binary_search_tree, opendsa:SearchStruct/BalancedTree). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Tree rotations
concepts.statement: rotateLeft(u) and rotateRight(u) restructure a node and one child in O(1) while preserving the BST property, moving one node up and the other down.

concepts.name: Build a perfectly balanced BST from a sorted array
concepts.statement: Gather a subtree's nodes into array a by in-order traversal (packIntoArray), then make a[m] (m = a.length/2) the root and build both halves recursively (buildBalanced); O(size(u)) time and minimum height.

concepts.name: Random binary search trees
concepts.statement: Inserting a uniformly random permutation of 0..n-1 into a BST yields a random BST: the expected search path for x is H_{x+1} + H_{n-x} - O(1) (and H_{x+1} + H_{n-x} for an absent value), so it can be built in O(n log n) and find takes O(log n) expected time. Key step: a key i < x is on x's search path exactly when i comes first among {i,...,floor(x)} in the permutation, which happens with probability 1/(floor(x)-i+1).

concepts.name: Priority queue
concepts.statement: An abstract collection supporting insert and removal of the highest-priority (max or min) item.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:priority-queue, ods:priority-queue-interface).

concepts.name: Eytzinger layout (implicit binary tree in an array)
concepts.statement: Store a complete binary tree in an array in breadth-first order: root at 0, left(i) = 2i+1, right(i) = 2i+2, parent(i) = (i-1)/2.

concepts.name: Heap property
concepts.statement: In a (min-)heap the value stored at every non-root index i is not smaller than the value at parent(i), so the root a[0] holds the minimum.

concepts.name: Binary heap
concepts.statement: A complete binary tree stored in an array, where each parent is at least (max-heap) its children; children of index i sit at 2i+1 and 2i+2.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:binary-heap, ods:binary-heap).

concepts.name: Sift up and sift down
concepts.statement: Insert appends and sifts up; extract-max moves the last item to the root and sifts down; each is O(log n) because the tree height is O(log n).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:heap-sift, wikipedia:Binary_heap#Heap_operations). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Linear-time heapify
concepts.statement: Sifting down every internal node from the last to the root turns an arbitrary array into a heap in O(n), not O(n log n).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:build-heap, ods:bottom-up-heapify).

concepts.name: Heapsort
concepts.statement: Heapify the array, then repeatedly swap the max to the end and sift down, sorting in place in O(n log n); it is not stable.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:heapsort, ods:heap-sort).

concepts.name: Implement a max-heap
concepts.statement: Build insert, sift_up, get_max, get_size, is_empty, extract_max, sift_down, remove(i), heapify and heap_sort.

concepts.name: Random walks in binary trees
concepts.statement: A walk from the root that goes to a random child at each step until it falls off the tree has expected length at most log(n+1) in any binary tree with n nodes.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:random-walk-binary-tree, cpa:randomized-heap-bound). Source tiers differ (ods stretch, cpa contest); reconciled to the most common, stretch. Edge to meldable-heap dropped: cpa proves the random root-to-leaf path bound inside its randomized-heap article; ODS states it as a lemma about any binary tree, and the heap rests on it, not the reverse. Breaks a cycle.

concepts.name: MeldableHeap (randomized meldable heap)
concepts.statement: A heap-ordered binary tree with no shape constraint; merge(h1,h2) keeps the smaller root and recursively merges the other heap into a randomly chosen child. add and remove are merges, each O(log n) expected.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:meldable-heap, cpa:randomized-heap). Source tiers differ (ods stretch, cpa contest); reconciled to the most common, stretch.

concepts.name: Comparison-based sorting
concepts.statement: A sorting algorithm that examines elements only through compare(a,b), so it works for any data type; merge-sort, quicksort and heap-sort sort into non-decreasing order in O(n log n) (expected) time.

concepts.name: Stability in sorting
concepts.statement: A sort is stable if items with equal keys keep their original relative order (merge sort is; quicksort and heapsort usually are not).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:sort-stability, wikipedia:Sorting_algorithm#Stability). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Selection sort
concepts.statement: Repeatedly select the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it into place; O(n^2) in every case.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:selection-sort, wikipedia:Selection_sort, opendsa:Sorting/SelectionSort). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Insertion sort
concepts.statement: Insert each item into the sorted prefix by shifting larger items right; O(n^2) average and worst, O(n) on nearly sorted input, stable.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:insertion-sort, wikipedia:Insertion_sort, opendsa:Sorting/InsertionSort). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Bubble sort
concepts.statement: Repeatedly swap adjacent out-of-order pairs; O(n^2).
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:bubble-sort, wikipedia:Bubble_sort, opendsa:Sorting/BubbleSort). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: The divide-and-conquer pattern
concepts.statement: Divide the instance into smaller independent instances, delegate each to recursion, and combine their solutions; with a base case for constant-size inputs.

concepts.name: Solving recurrences by guess and confirm
concepts.statement: Guess a closed form (from small cases or a recursion tree) and prove it by induction, adjusting constants or lower-order terms when the induction fails; worked for Hanoi, Fibonacci and mergesort.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of recursion-trees (core).

concepts.name: Recursion trees and the master theorem
concepts.statement: To solve T(n)=rT(n/c)+f(n), sum the work level by level: if level sums decrease geometrically the root dominates (O(f(n))), if equal it is O(f(n) log n), if increasing the leaves dominate (O(n^{log_c r})).
aliases: Recurrence relations and the master theorem
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe:recursion-trees, jeffe-notes:recursion-tree-method, ciu:recurrences-master-theorem). CIU's master-theorem row joins Erickson's recursion-tree method: the master theorem's three cases are read off the recursion tree.

concepts.name: The Akra-Bazzi method
concepts.statement: For T(n) = sum a_i T(n/b_i) + f(n), let rho satisfy sum a_i b_i^{-rho} = 1; then T(n) = Theta(n^rho (1 + integral_1^n f(u)/u^{rho+1} du)).

concepts.name: Linear recurrences by annihilators
concepts.statement: Write the recurrence with shift operators; the operator that annihilates the sequence factors as a product of (E - c) terms, and each factor (E - c)^k contributes a term polynomial(n) * c^n to the solution.

concepts.name: Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.statement: Two n-digit numbers can be multiplied with three recursive half-size multiplications instead of four, giving O(n^{log_2 3}) = O(n^1.585) time.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe:karatsuba, ciu:karatsuba).

concepts.name: Mergesort
concepts.statement: Split the array in halves, sort each recursively, and merge the sorted halves in linear time; correctness follows by induction and the running time satisfies T(n)=2T(n/2)+O(n)=O(n log n).
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe:mergesort, ciu:mergesort, ods:merge-sort). Edge to merge-sorted-sequences added: merge sort repeats the two-list merge, which chapter 2 teaches as a two-pointer case (gap inventory).

concepts.name: Sorting linked lists versus arrays
concepts.statement: Which sorts suit which structures: merge sort works on linked lists without random access; quicksort and heapsort want arrays.

concepts.name: In-place partition around a pivot
concepts.statement: Partition rearranges A[1..n] in place in O(n) time so that elements smaller than the pivot precede it and larger ones follow, returning the pivot's final index.

concepts.name: In-place three-way partitioning
concepts.statement: Scan the subarray with three indices so that, at the end, a[i..p] < x, a[p+1..q-1] = x and a[q..i+n-1] > x, swapping elements into place without extra arrays.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:three-way-partition, wikipedia:Dutch_national_flag_problem#The_array_case). Also the Dutch national flag problem, a three-pointer case of the two-pointer pattern (2.3); the Wikipedia treatment is from the gap-patterns run (§1).

concepts.name: Quicksort
concepts.statement: Choose a pivot, partition the array around it, and recursively sort both sides; worst case O(n^2) with bad pivots, O(n log n) if the pivot is always near the median.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe:quicksort, ciu:quicksort, ods:quicksort).

concepts.name: The nuts and bolts problem
concepts.statement: Given n nuts and n bolts that can only be compared to each other, pick a random bolt, partition the nuts with it and the bolts with its matching nut, and recurse: expected O(n log n) comparisons, mirroring randomized quicksort.

concepts.name: Expected comparisons of randomized quicksort
concepts.statement: The i-th and j-th smallest elements are compared iff one of them is the first pivot chosen among ranks i..j, with probability 2/(j-i+1); summing gives at most 2n H_n = O(n log n) expected comparisons.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe-notes:quicksort-expected-comparisons, ods:quicksort-analysis).

concepts.name: Implement merge sort and quicksort
concepts.statement: Write merge sort and quicksort and state the best, average and worst cost of each sort studied.

concepts.name: Quickselect
concepts.statement: To find the k-th smallest element, partition around a pivot and recurse only into the side containing rank k; worst case O(n^2), linear if pivots are good.
aliases: Quickselect for the k-th order statistic
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (jeffe:quickselect, ciu:quickselect, cpa:quickselect).

concepts.name: Linear-time selection (median of medians)
concepts.statement: Choosing the pivot as the median of the medians of groups of five guarantees each side has at most about 7n/10 elements, giving T(n) <= T(n/5)+T(7n/10)+O(n) = O(n).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe:median-of-medians, cpa:median-of-medians). Source tiers differ (jeffe stretch, cpa contest); reconciled to the most common, stretch.

concepts.name: Decision-tree lower bounds
concepts.statement: A comparison algorithm corresponds to a decision tree whose internal nodes are queries and leaves are outputs; its worst-case running time is at least the tree's depth.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of information-theoretic-bound (core).

concepts.name: Information-theoretic lower bound
concepts.statement: A decision tree with branching factor k that must distinguish N outcomes has depth at least log_k N; e.g. searching a sorted array needs Omega(log n) comparisons. Hashing escapes it by asking queries with more than O(1) outcomes.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from stretch to core: it is a prerequisite of comparison-sort-lower-bound (core).

concepts.name: Lower bound for comparison sorting
concepts.statement: Any comparison-based sort needs Omega(n log n) comparisons in the worst case, so merge sort and heapsort are asymptotically optimal.
aliases: Comparison sorting needs Omega(n log n)
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:comparison-sort-lower-bound, ods:sorting-lower-bound, jeffe-notes:sorting-lower-bound).

concepts.name: Reductions to and from sorting
concepts.statement: Nuts and bolts and sorting reduce to each other, so randomized nuts-and-bolts matching needs Omega(n log n) comparisons and any deterministic O(n log n) solution would be hard to find.

concepts.name: Counting sort
concepts.statement: To sort n integers in {0..k-1}, count occurrences in c, take prefix sums so c[i] gives final positions, then place elements into output b scanning a from right to left (stable). O(n+k) time, beating the comparison bound because a[i] is used as an array index.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:counting-sort, ciu:linear-time-sorts). ciu:linear-time-sorts also treats radix-sort (row split by granularity). CIU's one row covers counting and radix sort; split, CIU's row treats both.

concepts.name: Radix sort
concepts.statement: Sort w-bit integers in w/d passes of counting sort on successive d-bit digits, least significant first, relying on stability; O((w/d)(n + 2^d)) time, so integers in {0..n^c-1} sort in O(cn) time.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:radix-sort, ciu:linear-time-sorts). ciu:linear-time-sorts also treats counting-sort (row split by granularity).

concepts.name: AVL tree
concepts.statement: A BST where subtree heights differ by at most one, restored by rotations, so search, insert and delete are O(log n); more rigidly balanced than red-black trees.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:avl-tree, wikipedia:AVL_tree, opendsa:SearchStruct/AVL). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: 2-3 search tree
concepts.statement: A perfectly balanced search tree whose nodes hold one or two keys (two or three children).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:2-3-tree, wikipedia:2–3_tree).

concepts.name: 2-3-4 tree
concepts.statement: A balanced search tree whose nodes hold one to three keys; its splits correspond to red-black colour flips and rotations.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:2-3-4-tree, ods:two-four-tree).

concepts.name: Adding and removing leaves in a 2-4 tree
concepts.statement: Adding a leaf may give a node 5 children; split it into nodes of 2 and 3 children and push the split up to the parent, possibly creating a new root. Removing a leaf may leave a node with 1 child; borrow from a sibling or merge with it, repeating upward.

concepts.name: Red-black tree properties
concepts.statement: A BST with each node red (0) or black (1), external nodes and root black, satisfying black-height (every root-to-leaf path has the same number of black nodes) and no-red-edge (no two adjacent reds). Its height is at most 2 log n.

concepts.name: Red-black trees simulate 2-4 trees
concepts.statement: Contracting every red node into its black parent turns a red-black tree into a 2-4 tree whose leaves are the external nodes, and each 2-4 node becomes a black node with up to two red children. This correspondence explains the black-height property and the 2 log n height bound.

concepts.name: Left-leaning red-black trees
concepts.statement: ODS's RedBlackTree also enforces the left-leaning property: if u.left is black then u.right is black. pushBlack(u)/pullBlack(u) move colour between a node and its children, and flipLeft/flipRight rotate while swapping colours.

concepts.name: Red-black insertion fixup
concepts.statement: add(x) inserts a red leaf, then addFixup(u) repairs red-red and left-leaning violations by flipLeft, flipRight and pushBlack while moving up the tree, mirroring a 2-4 tree split.

concepts.name: Red-black deletion fixup
concepts.statement: remove(x) splices out a node w with at most one child u (moving the successor's value into x's node if needed) and adds w.colour to u.colour, which can make u double-black or break left-leaning; removeFixup(u) moves the double-black up by rotations and recolourings in three cases (removeFixupCase1-3), mirroring 2-4 borrows and merges.

concepts.name: Red-black tree performance
concepts.statement: A BST with red/black node colouring rules that keep height at most 2 log n, giving worst-case O(log n) operations; equivalent to 2-3-4 trees.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:red-black-tree, ods:red-black-performance). Tier from CIU (optional list); other sources say ods core.

concepts.name: Treap
concepts.statement: Each node gets a random unique priority; the tree is a BST on keys and a heap on priorities, so its shape equals the random BST built in priority order and add, remove and find take O(log n) expected time.
concepts.notes: Merged 4 rows (ods:treap, ciu:treap, cpa:treap, jeffe-notes:treap). Tier from CIU (optional list); other sources say ods stretch, cpa contest, jeffe-notes stretch.

concepts.name: Treap insertion and deletion by rotation
concepts.statement: add(x) inserts a leaf as in a BST, then bubbleUp rotates it upward while its priority is smaller than its parent's; remove(x) trickleDown rotates x down toward the child of smaller priority until it is a leaf, then deletes it.
aliases: Treap insertion and deletion by rotations
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:treap-updates, jeffe-notes:treap-operations).

concepts.name: Random priorities give expected logarithmic depth
concepts.statement: With independent uniformly random priorities, node k is an ancestor of node i with probability 1/(|k-i|+1), so every node has expected depth at most 2 ln n + O(1).

concepts.name: Treap split and merge
concepts.statement: split(T, X) cuts a treap into keys <= X and > X, merge(T1, T2) joins treaps whose keys are ordered; both are O(log N) expected and insert, erase, build and union are written with them.

concepts.name: Building a treap in O(N) offline
concepts.statement: From sorted keys (or sorted (x,y) pairs, using a stack) a treap / Cartesian tree is built in linear time.

concepts.name: Implicit treap
concepts.statement: Use subtree sizes as implicit keys so a treap acts as an array supporting insert/erase anywhere, range aggregates, range add/paint and range reversal in O(log N).

concepts.name: Partial rebuilding
concepts.statement: Keep a tree balanced lazily: when some subtree becomes too unbalanced, destroy it and rebuild it perfectly balanced, charging the O(size) cost to the many updates that caused the imbalance.

concepts.name: Lazy deletion and global rebuilding
concepts.statement: Mark deleted nodes instead of removing them and rebuild the whole tree perfectly balanced once half the nodes are marked; rebuilding costs O(n) but is amortized O(1) per deletion.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from contest to stretch: it is a prerequisite of scapegoat-tree (stretch).

concepts.name: ScapegoatTree
concepts.statement: A BST with counters n and q (q/2 <= n <= q) whose height stays at most log_{3/2} q < log_{3/2} n + 2. When an insertion lands deeper than log_{3/2} q, climb to a scapegoat w with size(w)/size(parent(w)) > 2/3 and rebuild it; when q > 2n after a removal, rebuild the whole tree and set q = n. find is O(log n) worst case and rebuilds cost O(m log m) over m updates.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ods:scapegoat-tree, jeffe-notes:scapegoat-tree). Source tiers differ (ods stretch, jeffe-notes contest); reconciled to the most common, stretch.

concepts.name: Amortized analysis of scapegoat rebuilding
concepts.statement: Every node of depth h > log_{3/2} q has an ancestor w with size(w)/size(parent(w)) > 2/3; finding w and rebuilding it costs O(size(w)), paid by a credit scheme: each update gives one credit to every node on its path (at most log_{3/2} m credits), and a node needing a rebuild has accumulated Omega(size) credits since it was last balanced, giving O(m log m) total.

concepts.name: Rotations, double rotations and splaying
concepts.statement: Splaying moves a node to the root by zig, zig-zig and zig-zag (double) rotations, roughly halving the depth of every node on the access path.
concepts.notes: Tier raised from contest to stretch: it is a prerequisite of splay-tree (stretch).

concepts.name: Splay tree
concepts.statement: A self-adjusting BST that rotates each accessed key to the root, giving O(log n) amortized operations.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:splay-tree, jeffe-notes:splay-tree, opendsa:SearchStruct/Splay). Tier from CIU (optional list); other sources say jeffe-notes contest, opendsa stretch. Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Skiplist structure
concepts.statement: A sequence of singly-linked lists L_0..L_h where each element of L_{r-1} is promoted to L_r on a coin toss of heads; an element's height is the largest r with it in L_r (expected 1), a sentinel heads every list, and a search path runs from the sentinel in L_h down to any node in L_0.

concepts.name: Expected skiplist search path length
concepts.statement: The expected length of the search path to any node in L_0 is at most 2 log n + O(1). Nodes store an array next[] with one pointer per level, so x is stored once.

concepts.name: Skip list
concepts.statement: Layers of linked lists, each keeping a random half of the one below, give expected O(log n) search and insertion.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:skip-list, jeffe-notes:skip-list, ods:skiplist-sset).

concepts.name: SkiplistList (indexed skiplist)
concepts.statement: Each edge stores its length (number of L_0 edges it spans), so findPred(i) can navigate by index; get, set, add(i,x) and remove(i) take O(log n) expected time.

concepts.name: Skiplist size and height
concepts.statement: A skiplist on n elements has expected 2n nodes excluding sentinels and 2n + O(log n) including them, expected height at most log n + 2, and expected search path length at most 2 log n + O(1).

concepts.name: External memory model
concepts.statement: Data lives in external memory divided into blocks of B words; transferring a block costs one unit and computation in internal memory is free, so cost counts block reads and writes. A BlockStore offers readBlock, writeBlock, placeBlock and freeBlock.

concepts.name: K-ary tree
concepts.statement: A tree in which each node has at most k children (the branching factor).
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:k-ary-tree, wikipedia:M-ary_tree).

concepts.name: B-tree structure
concepts.statement: For B >= 2, all leaves have the same depth, every non-root internal node has between B and 2B children (the root 2 to 2B), and a node with k children stores k-1 sorted keys separating the children's subtrees. Height is O(log_B n).

concepts.name: B-tree search
concepts.statement: find(x) descends from the root; at each node binary search (findIt, O(log B)) finds the smallest key > x, continuing in that child, and the most recent such key z is returned as the successor when x is absent.

concepts.name: B-tree insertion with splits
concepts.statement: addRecursive inserts x into a leaf; a node that overflows to 2B keys (2B+1 children) is split: a new node w takes the B largest keys and the last B+1 children and the middle key moves up to the parent, possibly cascading to the root, which grows the tree by one level.

concepts.name: B-tree deletion with borrow and merge
concepts.statement: removeRecursive deletes from a leaf (replacing an internal key by the smallest in its right subtree); a node left with fewer than B-1 keys underflows, and checkUnderflow fixes it by borrowing keys from a sibling or merging with it; merges can cascade up and shrink the root.

concepts.name: B-tree
concepts.statement: A balanced k-ary search tree with large nodes sized to a disk block, keeping height O(log_B n); used by databases and filesystems.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:b-tree, ods:b-tree-performance).

concepts.name: Trie (R-way)
concepts.statement: A tree keyed by characters, where each path from the root spells a prefix, so lookup costs O(key length) regardless of how many keys are stored.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:trie, cpa:trie).

concepts.name: Trie prefix operations and performance
concepts.statement: Tries support prefix matching, longest-prefix and ordered key iteration; their cost depends on key length and alphabet size.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (ciu:trie-operations, wikipedia:Trie#Operations). Open prose added in the gap inventory from dossiers/sweep-dsa.md, Candidates.

concepts.name: Ternary search trie
concepts.statement: A trie whose nodes have three children (less, equal, greater) to save space over R-way nodes.

concepts.name: BinaryTrie
concepts.statement: Store w-bit integers as root-to-leaf paths of depth w (bit 0 left, 1 right); leaves form a doubly-linked list and a node missing a child keeps a jump pointer to the smallest or largest leaf in its subtree. add, remove and find (successor) take O(w) time; space O(nw).

concepts.name: XFastTrie
concepts.statement: Add one hash table per trie level holding the prefixes present; find(x) binary searches over prefix length for the deepest node on x's path, giving O(log w) expected find, while add and remove take O(w) expected; space O(nw).

concepts.name: YFastTrie
concepts.statement: Keep about one in w elements (each sampled with probability 1/w) in an XFastTrie and store the elements between consecutive samples in treaps of expected size at most 2w-1; add, remove and find take O(log w) expected time and space is O(n+w).

concepts.name: van Emde Boas trees
concepts.statement: A recursive structure over a universe of size u gives predecessor and successor queries in O(log log u).

concepts.name: Augmenting data structures
concepts.statement: Store extra information in each node (e.g. subtree size) and maintain it on updates to answer new queries such as order statistics.

concepts.name: k-d tree
concepts.statement: A binary tree splitting space on alternating coordinates, for range and nearest-neighbour queries over points.

concepts.name: Graph (directed, undirected, weighted)
concepts.statement: A set of vertices joined by edges, which may be directed or undirected and may carry weights.
concepts.notes: Merged 3 rows (ciu:graph, jeffe:graph-basics, ods:graph-definitions).

concepts.name: Modeling problems as graphs
concepts.statement: Many problems become graph problems once states or objects are vertices and allowed transitions or relations are edges (examples: maps, mazes, configuration graphs, word ladders).

concepts.name: Graph operations
concepts.statement: Typical operations are addEdge(i,j), removeEdge(i,j), hasEdge(i,j), outEdges(i) and inEdges(i); which representation is best depends on which operations the application needs fast.

concepts.name: Adjacency matrices
concepts.statement: An adjacency matrix is a V x V array with A[u,v]=1 iff uv is an edge; it uses Theta(V^2) space and tests adjacency in O(1) time.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe:adjacency-matrix, ods:adjacency-matrix).

concepts.name: Adjacency lists
concepts.statement: An adjacency list stores, for each vertex, a list of its neighbours; it uses O(V+E) space and lists the neighbours of v in O(deg(v)) time.
concepts.notes: Merged 2 rows (jeffe:adjacency-list, ods:adjacency-lists).

concepts.name: Graph representations
concepts.statement: Objects and pointers, adjacency matrix (O(V^2) space, O(1) edge test), adjacency list (O(V+E) space) and adjacency map each trade space against edge-query and iteration speed.
